sources.entry: Judge0 CE - API to compile and run source code. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Judge0 is an open-source, sandboxed online code execution system exposed through a JSON HTTP API, used to run untrusted or AI-generated code in many languages.
summary.what_it_does: Judge0 accepts source code plus optional stdin, language ID, compiler options, command-line arguments, and time and memory limits over a simple HTTP JSON API, and returns detailed execution results. It supports compiling and running multi-file programs (projects) and additional files alongside a single-file program. Execution is sandboxed so untrusted code can be run safely. The README states support for 90+ languages and lists webhooks (HTTP callbacks) as a feature. An official Python SDK is provided, and the project can be self-hosted or used as a managed cloud service. It ships in two flavors, Judge0 CE on the master branch and Judge0 Extra CE on the extra branch, which differ mainly in supported languages. The README also lists a research paper describing its architecture and many third-party projects that use it.
use_cases: Run user-submitted code in a competitive programming or online judge platform
Add a code execution backend to an online IDE or code editor
Execute AI-generated code safely as an agent tool
Automated grading of programming assignments in e-learning
how_to_run: Use the Judge0 Cloud via Rapid, or work directly with the Judge0 team for managed hosting
Self-host Judge0 on your own infrastructure (follow the documentation for installation)
Send a POST request with JSON containing language_id and source_code to the API endpoint
Or install the official Python SDK with: pip install judge0
notable: Sandboxed compilation and execution of untrusted code, built on Isolate
Supports multi-file projects and extra files alongside the main program
Simple HTTP JSON API plus an official Python SDK
Two flavors (CE and Extra CE) on separate branches with different language sets
Designed for scalable, modular deployment and described in a published research paper
caveats: Self-hosting requires setting up your own infrastructure; the README points to documentation for details
Managed cloud and some support options are offered by the project team, so availability and pricing are outside the repository
The README does not give hardware requirements or detailed platform limits
